claim.why_it_matters: The one four-row meta-language term table of 10.6.1 is split into two tables with the environment-division row left as a loose paragraph outside any table, and the second fragment turns options-paragraph into a header row; the content is all present but a table-reading tool would miss the environment-division mapping.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page (PDF p231, printed page 207, end of 10.6.1) shows one continuous Term/Subclause table with four rows: data-division 13; environment-division 12; options-paragraph 11.9; procedure-division 14. The rendered page-231.md has a table with header Term|Subclause and the single data-division row, then environment-division 12, Environment division as a loose paragraph, then a second table whose header row is options-paragraph|11.9 and whose only body row is procedure-division. The claim quotes both sources accurately. All the text is present and a human reader gets the same meaning, so this is not normative. It is a real structural defect, though: the table is split, one mapping sits outside any table, and a data row has become a header. A tool that reads the tables would lose or mislabel the environment-division and options-paragraph mappings. Severity structural is correct.
